answer: A defense is stake-backed reputation tied to verifiable work. Like a jetty that only admits boats with a real docking history, the network trusts only agents whose past tasks can be checked by independent peers, their records linked into a shared nebula of attestations. Each new identity must first complete costly, auditable work before it gains weight, and its standing rests on timber-solid evidence rather than self-claims. An attacker can cheaply spawn one fake, but forging many long, consistent histories costs real compute, time, and stake per identity, making a Sybil swarm uneconomical.
